name: parity-mcp

tools.name: verify_connection
tools.description: Check the configured Parity API key: confirms it is valid and reports its scopes plus the license status and plan. Call this first if any other tool fails with an auth error — the "scopes" list tells you exactly what this key is allowed to do.

tools.name: key_usage
tools.description: Metadata for the current API key (name, created/last-used, scopes) and the live per-minute rate-limit window state. Parity limits are 30 requests/minute per IP, shared across all scopes — there is no monthly quota.

tools.name: get_license
tools.description: This license's plan, status, expiry, server IP/port and player cap. Requires the license:read scope.

tools.name: get_config
tools.description: Read-only snapshot of the anti-cheat's current client/server detection configuration. Prefers a live read from the FiveM server and falls back to the last-known stored copy (response then has "stale": true). Requires the config:read scope.

tools.name: platform_stats
tools.description: Anonymised platform-wide aggregates across every Parity customer (active licenses, total bans issued, players tracked, latest anti-cheat version). No per-customer breakdown. Any valid key — no extra scope.

tools.name: get_player
tools.description: Look up one player the anti-cheat has seen at least once: profile, playtime, all known identifiers, ban count, stored risk level and admin notes. Requires the players:read scope.

identifier.description: A player identifier value: a Steam ID64 (17 digits), Discord user ID, Rockstar license hash, FiveM id, or IP address. The player must have connected to this server at least once — there is no way to address someone who never joined.

type.description: Narrows the lookup to one identifier kind. Omit to search every kind plus hardware tokens.

tools.name: analyze_player
tools.description: One-call intelligence bundle for a player: profile + identifiers + active bans + total ban history + threat score (riskLevel / suspicionScore / riskFactors). Use this for "is this player suspicious?". Requires the players:read scope.

identifier.description: A player identifier value: a Steam ID64 (17 digits), Discord user ID, Rockstar license hash, FiveM id, or IP address. The player must have connected to this server at least once — there is no way to address someone who never joined.

type.description: Narrows the lookup to one identifier kind. Omit to search every kind plus hardware tokens.

tools.name: get_player_threat_score
tools.description: Just the risk score Parity already computes for a player from Steam/Discord reputation and connection signals: riskLevel (LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH/CRITICAL), numeric suspicionScore, and the riskFactors that fed it. Requires the players:read scope.

identifier.description: A player identifier value: a Steam ID64 (17 digits), Discord user ID, Rockstar license hash, FiveM id, or IP address. The player must have connected to this server at least once — there is no way to address someone who never joined.

type.description: Narrows the lookup to one identifier kind. Omit to search every kind plus hardware tokens.

tools.name: find_alt_accounts
tools.description: Other players ON THIS SAME SERVER that share an identifier or hardware token with the given player — never crosses to another customer's data. Each result shows how many identifiers matched and whether that alt is banned. Requires the players:alts scope.

identifier.description: A player identifier value: a Steam ID64 (17 digits), Discord user ID, Rockstar license hash, FiveM id, or IP address. The player must have connected to this server at least once — there is no way to address someone who never joined.

type.description: Narrows the lookup to one identifier kind. Omit to search every kind plus hardware tokens.

tools.name: list_online_players
tools.description: Live snapshot of currently-connected players (id, name, ping, session time). The "id" here is the FiveM server id — use it as the `source` for test_rule. Requires the players:online scope and the FiveM server to be online.

tools.name: get_player_notes
tools.description: Read the internal free-text admin note stored on a player (same field as the dashboard player dialog). Requires the players:notes scope.

identifier.description: A player identifier value: a Steam ID64 (17 digits), Discord user ID, Rockstar license hash, FiveM id, or IP address. The player must have connected to this server at least once — there is no way to address someone who never joined.

type.description: Narrows the lookup to one identifier kind. Omit to search every kind plus hardware tokens.

tools.name: set_player_notes
tools.description: Overwrite a player's internal admin note (max 5000 chars). Replaces the whole note — read it first with get_player_notes if you want to append. Requires the players:notes scope.

identifier.description: A player identifier value: a Steam ID64 (17 digits), Discord user ID, Rockstar license hash, FiveM id, or IP address. The player must have connected to this server at least once — there is no way to address someone who never joined.

type.description: Narrows the lookup to one identifier kind. Omit to search every kind plus hardware tokens.

notes.description: The new note text. An empty string clears the note.

tools.name: kick_player
tools.description: Disconnect a currently-online player. Does NOT create a ban. Requires the players:kick scope and the FiveM server online (503 otherwise).

identifier.description: A player identifier value: a Steam ID64 (17 digits), Discord user ID, Rockstar license hash, FiveM id, or IP address. The player must have connected to this server at least once — there is no way to address someone who never joined.

type.description: Narrows the lookup to one identifier kind. Omit to search every kind plus hardware tokens.

reason.description: Shown to the player. Defaults to "Kicked by admin".

tools.name: message_player
tools.description: Send a chat message to a currently-online player via FiveM's chat resource. Requires the players:message scope and the server online.

identifier.description: A player identifier value: a Steam ID64 (17 digits), Discord user ID, Rockstar license hash, FiveM id, or IP address. The player must have connected to this server at least once — there is no way to address someone who never joined.

type.description: Narrows the lookup to one identifier kind. Omit to search every kind plus hardware tokens.

tools.name: ban_player
tools.description: Ban a player by identifier and best-effort kick them if they are online. Links every known identifier/token for that player to the ban (respecting the dashboard's configured ban identifier types). Does NOT blacklist hardware tokens (no fresh hardware snapshot outside a live session). If the player is already banned this is a no-op that returns the existing ban. Requires the players:ban scope. Destructive — confirm the identifier with get_player first.

identifier.description: A player identifier value: a Steam ID64 (17 digits), Discord user ID, Rockstar license hash, FiveM id, or IP address. The player must have connected to this server at least once — there is no way to address someone who never joined.

type.description: Narrows the lookup to one identifier kind. Omit to search every kind plus hardware tokens.

reason.description: Ban reason (required). Stored and shown in the dashboard.

isPermanent.description: true = permanent. Otherwise set expiresAt for a temp ban.

expiresAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when a temporary ban lifts, e.g. "2026-12-31T23:59:59Z".

tools.name: lookup_ban
tools.description: Find the currently-active ban (if any) tied to a player identifier or hardware/session token. Returns 404-style "no ban found" when the player is not banned. Requires the bans:read scope.

identifier.description: Identifier value (Steam ID64, Discord ID, license, IP, …) or a hardware token.

type.description: Narrows the lookup to one identifier kind. Omit to search every kind plus hardware tokens.

tools.name: get_ban
tools.description: Look up a single ban by its human-readable display ban ID (e.g. "BAN-1042" — the prefix is per-server). Requires the bans:read scope.

ban_id.description: The display ban ID as shown in the dashboard, e.g. "BAN-1042".

tools.name: list_bans
tools.description: Paginated ban list for this server. Filter by active state and/or one player. Requires the bans:list scope.

active.description: true = only active bans, false = only inactive. Omit for all.

identifier.description: Restrict to one player by identifier value.

type.description: Narrows the lookup to one identifier kind. Omit to search every kind plus hardware tokens.

tools.name: unban
tools.description: Revoke one ban by its display ban ID OR by a player identifier (exactly one, not both). Takes effect on the next connection attempt — no live push needed. Requires the bans:write scope.

identifier.description: Player identifier value — used when you do not have the ban ID.

type.description: Narrows the lookup to one identifier kind. Omit to search every kind plus hardware tokens.

reason.description: Recorded on the revoke, shown in the dashboard.

tools.name: unban_recent
tools.description: Revoke the most recently issued active bans for this server — the controlled companion to unban_all. Use after a misconfigured rule mass-banned players. Requires the bans:write scope.

count.description: How many of the newest active bans to revoke. Default 1, max 50.

minutes.description: Only revoke bans issued within the last N minutes.

tools.name: unban_all
tools.description: Revoke EVERY active ban for this server in one call. Extremely destructive. Always leaves an audit trail and posts a Discord webhook notice if one is configured. Requires the bans:write scope AND confirm:true in this call.

confirm.description: Must be exactly true. This is a mass unban — there is no undo.

tools.name: ban_stats
tools.description: Active vs. issued ban counts across 24h / 7d / 30d / all-time windows for this server. Optionally filter to one exact ban reason. Requires the analytics:read scope.

reason.description: Exact ban-reason string to filter by.

tools.name: ban_trends
tools.description: Bans grouped by reason over a 24h / 7d / 30d window. Requires the analytics:read scope.

tools.name: get_server_stats
tools.description: Live server stats: online player count, average ping, uptime. Requires the server:stats scope and the FiveM server online (503 otherwise).

tools.name: list_server_events
tools.description: Paginated feed of everything logged to the dashboard's Events tab: bans, kicks, detections, config changes, API actions. Filter by event type and/or one player. Requires the server:events scope. Do not poll this in a tight loop (rate limit).

identifier.description: Restrict to events about one player, by identifier value.

tools.name: get_analytics
tools.description: Aggregate ban/event counts, events-by-type breakdown and top ban reasons over a trailing window. Requires the analytics:read scope.

days.description: Trailing window in days. Default 7, max 90.

tools.name: list_whitelist
tools.description: List whitelisted players and their flags (adminAccess, masterAdmin, blacklistedWeapons). Reads from the live FiveM server config. Requires the whitelist:read scope and the server online.

tools.name: add_whitelist
tools.description: Add a player to the whitelist. Pushes the updated config straight to the live FiveM server. Requires the whitelist:write scope and the server online. Note: masterAdmin / adminAccess grant in-game admin powers — only set them deliberately.

playerName.description: Display label for the dashboard list.

adminAccess.description: Grants in-game admin menu access. Default false.

masterAdmin.description: Grants full in-game admin. Default false.

blacklistedWeapons.description: Exempts the player from weapon blacklist enforcement. Default false.

tools.name: remove_whitelist
tools.description: Remove a player from the whitelist by their "<type>:<value>" identifier. Pushes the updated config to the live server. Requires the whitelist:write scope and the server online.

tools.name: list_team_members
tools.description: List this server's team members with roles, status (PENDING/ACTIVE) and permission maps. The license owner is not a team member row — see get_license for owner-tier info. Requires the team:read scope.

tools.name: invite_team_member
tools.description: Invite someone to the team by Discord ID. Creates a PENDING member — they must log in and accept the invite from Profile Settings before it becomes ACTIVE. Requires the team:write scope.

permissions.description: Permission map, e.g. {"banManagement": true, "viewLogs": true}. The teamManagement / teamManagementInvite permissions are always forced off via the API — grant those in the dashboard only.

tools.name: update_team_member
tools.description: Replace a team member's permission map. Cannot touch the OWNER row. Requires the team:write scope.

member_id.description: The team member id from list_team_members.

permissions.description: The full new permission map (replaces the old one).

tools.name: remove_team_member
tools.description: Remove a team member by id. Cannot remove the OWNER. Requires the team:write scope.

member_id.description: The team member id from list_team_members.

tools.name: rule_authoring_guide
tools.description: The Custom API Rules authoring reference: the flat-rule JSON schema, export-condition syntax, the whitelisting recipe, and the common gotchas. Read this before hand-writing a rule with upsert_rules or replace_rules.

tools.name: list_detections
tools.description: The catalogue of every valid detectionType, with triggerSource, default action and a description. Rows where isModuleWrapper is true are NOT valid rule targets — target one of their sub-checks instead. Requires the rules:read scope.

trigger_source.description: Filter to client- or server-side detections.

search.description: Case-insensitive substring match on detectionType / label / description.

tools.name: get_rules
tools.description: Read this server's current Custom API Rules set and the safeMode flag. Read this before any edit — writes replace the whole set. "stale": true means the FiveM server was offline and this is the last-stored copy. Requires the rules:read scope.

tools.name: test_rule
tools.description: Dry-run the current rule set against a currently-online player for one detectionType. Fires NO action — returns a trace of which rules matched and what would have happened. Get a `source` id from list_online_players. Requires the rules:read scope and the FiveM server online. Leave trigger_source unset and it is resolved from the detection's catalogue entry — a client-side detection is dry-run in the target player's game client, a server-side one in-process. Passing the wrong one (or letting it default to "server" for a client detection) makes the trace come back with zero rule groups.

source.description: The player's live FiveM server id (from list_online_players).

trigger_source.description: Omit to use the detection's own type from list_detections (recommended).

tools.name: upsert_rules
tools.description: Add or update rules by id, leaving every other existing rule untouched (reads the current set, merges on id, writes it back). New rule ids are stored DISABLED unless activate:true, so you can draft a rule for the owner to review. Requires the rules:write scope. Call rule_authoring_guide first if you are unsure of the shape.

id.description: Unique id within the rule set. Reusing an id overwrites that rule.

name.description: Shown in the dashboard rule list.

triggerSource.description: Must match the detection's own type from list_detections.

detectionType.description: A detectionType from list_detections (never a module-wrapper key), or "" to match every detection.

blockDetection.description: true suppresses Parity's own default ban/kick/log for this detection.

gateId.description: Shared by every action object of one logical trigger; "" = ungated.

order.description: Execution order, ascending across the whole set.

activate.description: true = newly-added rule ids are stored enabled. Default false.

tools.name: replace_rules
tools.description: REPLACE the entire Custom API Rules set. Anything not included is DELETED. Prefer upsert_rules / delete_rules for incremental changes. New rule ids are stored DISABLED unless activate_new:true. Requires the rules:write scope.

id.description: Unique id within the rule set. Reusing an id overwrites that rule.

name.description: Shown in the dashboard rule list.

triggerSource.description: Must match the detection's own type from list_detections.

detectionType.description: A detectionType from list_detections (never a module-wrapper key), or "" to match every detection.

blockDetection.description: true suppresses Parity's own default ban/kick/log for this detection.

gateId.description: Shared by every action object of one logical trigger; "" = ungated.

order.description: Execution order, ascending across the whole set.

safe_mode.description: true disables every custom rule on this server (panic switch).

activate_new.description: true = rules with a new id are stored enabled. Default false.

tools.name: delete_rules
tools.description: Remove rules by id (reads the current set, drops the given ids, writes the rest back). Requires the rules:write scope.

tools.name: set_safe_mode
tools.description: Turn safeMode on or off. safeMode:true disables EVERY Custom API Rule on this server at once without deleting anything — a panic switch. Leaves the rules themselves unchanged. Requires the rules:write scope.

tools.name: whitelist_detection
tools.description: High-level shortcut for the most common need: stop a detection from punishing a specific group of players (e.g. admins on duty). Builds a single SERVER rule — blockDetection:true, actionType:none, gated on a server-side export from one of your resources that returns true for the players to exempt — and upserts it. Server-side so the export can do a real identity/permission check (the player server id is passed as arg 1). Works for every detection, client-reported ones included. Stored DISABLED unless activate:true. Requires the rules:write scope. You still need the matching export in one of your own resources (see rule_authoring_guide).

detection_type.description: A detectionType from list_detections (a sub-check, never a module wrapper).

export_check.description: The SERVER-side export call that decides who is exempt, e.g. "exports['my_admin']:isParityWhitelisted()". With () and no args the player server id is passed as arg 1.

trigger_source.description: Defaults to "server" (recommended). Only pass "client" for an early client-side block with a client-side export.

export_value.description: Value the export must return to exempt the player. Default "true".

activate.description: true = enable immediately. Default false (draft for review).

tools.name: whitelist_all_detections
tools.description:
Build ONE catch-all rule that hands every detection to a single server-side export and lets that export decide. Rule: detectionType "" (matches every detection), triggerSource "server", blockDetection:true, actionType:none, gated on exports[<resource>]:<fn>(source, detectionType, details) == true. When your export returns true the detection's default ban/kick/log is suppressed; return false and it proceeds. Your export gets:
  - source: player server id
  - detectionType: e.g. "teleport", "aimbotHitrate", "weaponDamageModifier"
  - details: a table with detectionType, reason, and the detection-specific fields (distance, weapon, entity, …)
Put all your allow/deny logic in that one Lua function instead of dozens of rules. Prefer this over many whitelist_detection calls. Stored DISABLED unless activate:true. Requires the rules:write scope.

export_resource.description: Resource that owns the decision export, e.g. "my_admin".

export_function.description: Server-side export name, e.g. "parityIsAllowed". It is called as fn(source, detectionType, details).

activate.description: true = enable immediately. Default false (draft for review).
